Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testIsAvailableLocale()` fails with a NullPointerException in the method `isAvailableLocale(Locale)`. Inspecting the method `isAvailableLocale` reveals that it directly calls `cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale)`. The field `cAvailableLocaleSet` is a private static Set declared as `private static Set cAvailableLocaleSet;` but is never explicitly initialized at declaration or in a constructor.

The method `availableLocaleSet()` lazily initializes `cAvailableLocaleSet` if it is null, by creating a new unmodifiable set and assigning it to `cAvailableLocaleSet`. It then returns the set. 

The problem arises because `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` directly uses `cAvailableLocaleSet` without checking or invoking `availableLocaleSet()` first to ensure initialization. If no prior call to `availableLocaleSet()` occurred, `cAvailableLocaleSet` remains null, leading to a NullPointerException when calling `contains()` on it.

The failing test calls both `availableLocaleSet()` and `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` methods. If the test or any usage calls `isAvailableLocale` before `availableLocaleSet()`, it will cause NullPointerException.

Thus, the root cause is the unsafe use of the lazily-initialized static field `cAvailableLocaleSet` in the method `isAvailableLocale()` without guaranteeing it is initialized.

No relevant information is found in the recent bug reports for this issue. The solution would be either to ensure initialization of `cAvailableLocaleSet` before use or modify `isAvailableLocale()` to call `availableLocaleSet()` internally to guarantee initialization.

The test failure matches the reported description in the bug report about a potential NullPointerException when using `cAvailableLocaleSet` directly without initialization.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
